name: British Army in North America
troop_source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Monmouth : "first division, which comprised some 10,000 troops" and "second division ... just over 9,000 personnel" (army marching from Philadelphia, June 1778). For Charleston: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Charleston : "sailed southward with 8,500 troops and 5,000 sailors" (+2,500 under Rawdon on 18 April).

rows.label: Boston (arrives with Howe and Burgoyne)
rows.quote: Henry Clinton arrived on May 25 aboard HMS Cerberus

rows.label: Battle of Bunker Hill
rows.quote: followed himself to help rally the troops
rows.note: Clinton crossed to Charlestown with reserves for the third assault; battle date from same article.

rows.label: Cape Fear (awaits Cornwallis's convoy)
rows.quote: Clinton arrived at Cape Fear on March 12

rows.label: Off Charleston harbor
rows.quote: arrived outside Charles Town Harbor the next day
rows.note: Squadron weighed anchor at Cape Fear May 31; the article does not name Clinton in that sentence, he sailed with the squadron.

rows.label: Landing on Long Island, SC (now Isle of Palms)
rows.quote: Clinton began landing 2,200 troops on Long Island
rows.note: Long Island, SC is today's Isle of Palms.

rows.label: Battle of Sullivan's Island (attempted crossing)
rows.quote: General Clinton began movements to cross over to the northern end
rows.note: Battle date June 28 from the same article.

rows.label: Staten Island (arrives from the south)
rows.quote: On August 1, 45 ships arrived with generals Henry Clinton

rows.label: Gravesend Bay landing
rows.quote: advance guard of 4,000 British troops left Staten Island under the command of Clinton

rows.label: Battle of Long Island (Jamaica Pass flank march)
rows.quote: Clinton was to command the advance guard of the main army

rows.label: Pell's Point landing
rows.quote: Clinton's advance guard of 4,000 British light infantry and Hessian
rows.note: Date of the landing from the same article; Henry Clinton article says he led the army ashore in Westchester County.

rows.label: White Plains (commands British right)
rows.quote: British troops on the right under General Henry Clinton

rows.label: Newport (occupied)
rows.quote: which they did without opposition on December 8
rows.note: Same article says Howe detached Clinton with 6,000 men to occupy Newport.

rows.label: Fort Montgomery (Hudson Highlands)
rows.quote: On the foggy morning of October 6, Sir Henry Clinton landed 2,100 men
rows.note: Landed at Stony Point, marched on Forts Montgomery and Clinton the same day.

rows.label: Philadelphia (takes over from Howe)
rows.quote: That same day, General Clinton took over as commander-in-chief
rows.note: Henry Clinton article says only 'May 1778'; this date is from the William Howe article.

rows.label: Allentown (march across New Jersey)
rows.quote: On June 24, the first division arrived at Allentown
rows.note: Article says Clinton accompanied the first division.

rows.label: Battle of Monmouth
rows.quote: Clinton disengaged when he found Washington in an unassailable defensive position

rows.label: Newport (relief of the garrison)
rows.quote: relief force of Clinton and Grey arrived at Newport on September 1

rows.label: Philipsburg Manor (headquarters)
rows.quote: On 30 June 1779, Clinton issued what has become known as
rows.note: Proclamation issued from his headquarters at the Philipsburg Manor House, Westchester County.

rows.label: New York (sails south for Charleston)
rows.quote: the day after Christmas 1779, Clinton and his second-in-command
rows.note: Article says they sailed southward; Henry Clinton article says from New York.

rows.label: Savannah River (fleet anchors)
rows.quote: the fleet anchored in the Savannah River on 1 February 1780
rows.note: Position approximate: Tybee Island at the river mouth.

rows.label: James Island (crosses Stono River)
rows.quote: By 24 February, the British had crossed the Stono River onto James Island
rows.note: Army movement; Clinton led the expedition.

rows.label: Siege of Charleston begins
rows.quote: Clinton began a siege on 1 April

rows.label: Charleston surrenders
rows.quote: On May 12, Lincoln formally surrendered 3,371 men to the British
rows.note: Clinton was in command at the siege; some sources date the fall May 11 (negotiations began May 11, surrender May 12 per Wikipedia).
